sources.title: Higham and Alves, The Southeast Asian prehistoric house (2025)
sources.note: Direct full publisher text. Introduction identifies the language family and proposed farming dispersals; Section 6 documents mat impressions at Lo Gach circa 2750 BP. The proposed correlation does not assign a recoverable language to every excavated site. Public map observations come from local decoded atlas geometry, not this article.

sources.title: Barron and colleagues, MicroCT reveals domesticated rice within early Neolithic pottery (2017)
sources.note: Direct full text, Introduction, Methods and Results, especially Figures 1 and 2. Domesticated spikelet bases are identified in An Son and Loc Giang pottery; none in the one Rach Nui sherd. Methods used small offcuts before scanning, so do not claim no sampling damage. Dates are calibrated BP, with BP anchored to 1950.

sources.title: Wang and colleagues, Rice and millet cultivated in Ha Long Bay of Northern Vietnam 4000 years ago (2022)
sources.note: Direct publisher text. Abstract, Results and Discussion distinguish cereal-focused Trang Kenh from Bai Ben and Bai Cat Don plant use; microremains support interpretation of food use, not the ethnicity of individuals. DOI and PMC9666789 are the same work.

sources.title: Castillo and colleagues, Hunter-gatherer specialization in the Late Neolithic of southern Vietnam: the case of Rach Nui (online 2017; volume 2018)
sources.note: Direct 32-page author manuscript. Section 3.1 and Discussion identify rice, millet, gathered plants and probable exchange; evidence for local cultivation is lacking, not disproved. Sections on salinity do not establish ancient wells or toilets. Printed manuscript pages 6 to 9 and 12 to 13.

sources.title: Grono and colleagues, Early settlement construction: lime mortar floors at Loc Giang (2022)
sources.note: Direct publisher article; abstract, Loc Giang background, Results and Discussion; Figure 4. Floor sequence dates circa 3510 to 3150 cal BP, distinct from longer overall site dates. Minimal debris and repairs support cleaning and upkeep; sweeping or mats is an interpretation, not surviving household instructions.

sources.title: Tilley and Oxenham, Survival against the odds: care provision in Neolithic Vietnam (2011)
sources.note: ANU institutional original indexed full passages verified, direct download failed. International Journal of Paleopathology 1, pages 35 to 42, especially introduction and Sections 2.1.1, 2.1.2 and 2.2.1. M9 care is an explicit bioarchaeological inference from impairment and survival, not an excavated medical record. Exact caregivers, facilities and remedies are not known.

sources.title: Higham, Douka and Higham, A new chronology for the Bronze Age of northeastern Thailand (2015)
sources.note: Direct publisher text, abstract, regional significance and Supporting Figures S4 to S8. Short chronology is identified as the authors’ radiocarbon model, not all Southeast Asia sharing one change date. Wealthy infant graves suggest inherited status; no assumed pan-regional monarchy. The November 2015 correction concerns acknowledgments.

sources.title: SEAlang Library Khmer dictionary: ទឹក, tɨk, water
sources.note: Indexed original checked twice: first headword ទឹក tɨk, definition 1 noun water, liquid, juice. Direct page failed; original indexed text is the access witness. Modern dictionary sample accessed in 2026, not an inscription or a reconstructed Neolithic utterance.

sources.title: SEAlang Library: source editions of the Khmer dictionary
sources.note: Indexed original library resource description: primarily Headley and colleagues’ Cambodian-English dictionaries of 1977 and 1997, plus Chuon Nath material. The API combines resources; do not assign this individual headword uniquely to the 1997 edition. Combined with the query page as one underlying dictionary work for budgets.

proposedOverrides.name: Austroasiatic rice cultures
proposedOverrides.summary: Distinct archaeological communities and a language-family hypothesis, not a single rice-farming state.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One distinct contextual card, no aliases. Exact indexed culture spans circa 2000 to 323 BCE. Decoded 2000 BCE polygon includes a sample in Afghanistan and excludes Trang Kenh; public opening flags gross geographic mismatch. Language-family membership is not inferred automatically from material culture or rice consumption. Later Funan, Dvaravati, Khmer and Vietnamese dossiers remain separate.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: identities.json and point-checks.json; all phases are approximate organizational intervals with exclusive ends, not first settlement dates or universal technological transitions.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No excavated Neolithic writing, school, hospital, sewer or toilet attributed to this umbrella. Modern Khmer is a dated later dictionary example. Man Bac hygiene describes modeled assistance, not surviving facilities.
